content:
- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts often peak too early or too high after recent spikes, then sharply drop — suggesting overshoot and failure to capture mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices during sustained downward trends or when recent history shows consolidation.
- Forecast bias is more pronounced in high-price regimes (e.g., >85) — model tends to overreact to short-term volatility.
- Model fails to adjust for strong downward momentum in the 10–15 day window before the forecast horizon — lagged response to recent price drops.
- When true outcome shows sharp upward movement, model often misses the momentum or overcorrects downward.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the first 5–7 days of forecast — may be overfitting recent volatility or ignoring long-term trends.
- In low-price regimes (e.g., <80), model underestimates the true price, often by 2–5 points — may be underweighting risk or missing supply/demand shifts.
- Model does not adequately capture the “reversion to mean” behavior after sharp spikes — tends to hold high values longer than observed.
- Forecast error is more severe when true price moves >3% from prior 7-day average — model struggles with volatility clustering.
